text:
ana: Nightly eval alert: prompt_set 'user_sim_v2' regression — BLEU down 7 points and output diversity jumped. Putting samples here.

mike_r: Can you paste a few failed generations and the nightly config? :eyes:

ana: Sure — two samples (truncated):
1) "The capital of France is London."
2) "To bake a cake, first boil the flour..."
These are from run id 2026-03-18_03:12.

ana: Nightly config snippet: ```
model: gptq-7b-v3
sampler: default
params:
  temperature: 0.18
  top_p: 0.92
  top_k: 40
  seed: null
```

lucy: Wait we usually ship evals with temp=0.0 for deterministic checks, right? That config looks like a stray nonzero temp. :thinking:

eval-bot: [system] nightly-eval v2 finished, 1800 tests, 62 failures. Config hash: 0a7f9d3. Commit: 4b7e2c9. Linked PR: #8912

mike_r: @eval-bot can you attach the exact commit that produced that config hash? I want the changelog.

eval-bot: Attached: https://git.redwood/infra/commits/4b7e2c9 - change: sampler: switch default to "stochastic" when model supports KV caching.

devin: That lines up. We merged the runtime change last week; it flips sampler default for quantized pipelines to avoid cache underutilization. Might have accidentally made eval infra inherit it.

sam_k: There's also an RNG hotspot in the quant kernel that seeds based on process uptime when seed=null. If we used null seed for deterministic tests before but the runtime moved to nonzero default temp, combined effect could be worse.

lucy: Quick repro idea: run local eval harness forcing seed=12345 and temp=0.0 vs temp=0.18 and compare diffs. If seed-fixed + temp=0 keeps behavior stable, it's sampler param causing it.

ana: Running quick reproducer now locally (small batch). Logs:```
[2026-03-18 09:02:11] model=gptq-7b-v3 params={temp:0.0, top_p:1.0, top_k:0} -> PASS
[2026-03-18 09:02:35] model=gptq-7b-v3 params={temp:0.18, top_p:0.92, top_k:40} -> FAIL (mismatch tokens at idx 3)
``` 

mike_r: That strongly implicates sampler defaults. Two parallel actions: 1) revert the eval infra change so nightly keeps deterministic settings; 2) schedule a canary that tests stochastic defaults across the dev fleet.

devin: I'll open a revert PR for the eval runner and add an explicit override to keep temp=0.0 for deterministic suites. PR in 10min.

sam_k: I'll instrument the quant kernel RNG to log seed provenance for a few runs — want to be sure 'null' isn't becoming high-entropy runtime-dependent seeds.

ana: Thanks. I'll kick off a targeted bisect over commits touching infra/sampler and infra/eval-runner and paste results here.

lucy: If bisect narrows to the runtime change, we should also update docs and add a guard in the console to show when stochastic defaults are enabled for a route.

mike_r: Agreed. Keep notes minimal in the PRs. Triage owners: @devin for infra revert, @sam_k for kernel logs, @ana for bisect + sample set. Follow-up meeting if we don't have root cause by EOD. :thumbsup:
